title: Google Maps can now order your food, book your hotel, and read your calendar. Ask Maps just became an agent.
excerpt: Google Maps' Ask Maps gains agentic features: food ordering via Uber Eats/Toast/Square, hotel booking, event tickets. Personal Intelligence pulls from Gmail and Calendar.
content_html:
TL;DR

Google Maps’ Ask Maps gains agentic features: food ordering, hotel booking, event tickets. Personal Intelligence connects Gmail and Calendar for personalised answers. Rolling out in the US.

Google Maps is no longer just giving directions. The company announced on Thursday that Ask Maps, the Gemini-powered conversational feature it launched in March, is gaining agentic capabilities that let it order food, book hotels, and find event tickets. Users can describe what they want in natural language, and Ask Maps will surface options, populate a cart, and hand off payment to partner platforms including Uber Eats, Toast, and Square.

The hotel booking flow works similarly. A user can type something like “find me a top-rated hotel with an artsy vibe near a gym in downtown Miami for next weekend,” and Ask Maps will compare prices and check availability before presenting options. Users click through to a partner’s website to complete the booking. Event discovery follows the same pattern: ask about comedy shows or live music nearby and Ask Maps returns options with links to buy tickets. The new agentic features are rolling out in the US.

The more significant addition is Personal Intelligence, which connects Ask Maps to a user’s Gmail and Google Calendar. With permission, the feature can reference flight details, dinner reservations, or conference schedules sitting in a user’s inbox to provide tailored recommendations without the user spelling out every detail. It is off by default. Ask Maps will also now remember prior conversations, so users can pick up trip planning where they left off. A live transit widget that tracks delays in real time is also rolling out.

The update is the clearest example yet of Google turning its products into agents that complete tasks rather than just answer questions. At I/O in May, Google replaced the search box with AI agents that monitor the web, build custom tools, and act on a user’s behalf. Ask Maps is now doing the same thing inside a navigation app used by over a billion people monthly. The question is whether users will trust a map to order their lunch, and whether the restaurants, hotels, and ticketing platforms on the other end of those handoffs will see it as distribution or disintermediation.

content_html_zh:
TL;DR

谷歌地图的 Ask Maps 获得了代理功能：食品订购、酒店预订、活动门票。 个人智能连接 Gmail 和日历以获得个性化答案。 在美国推出。

谷歌地图不再只是提供方向。 该公司周四宣布，Ask Maps（该公司于 3 月份推出的由 Gemini 驱动的对话功能）正在获得代理功能，使其能够订购食物、预订酒店和查找活动门票。 用户可以用自然语言描述他们想要什么，Ask Maps 将显示选项、填充购物车，并将付款交给 Uber Eats、Toast 和 Square 等合作伙伴平台。

酒店预订流程类似。 用户可以输入诸如“下周末在迈阿密市中心一家健身房附近为我寻找一家具有艺术氛围的顶级酒店”之类的内容，“Ask Maps”会在提供选择之前比较价格并检查空房情况。 用户点击进入合作伙伴的网站即可完成预订。 活动发现遵循相同的模式：询问附近的喜剧表演或现场音乐，“询问地图”会返回带有购买门票链接的选项。 新的代理功能正在美国推出。

更重要的补充是个人智能，它将 Ask Maps 连接到用户的 Gmail 和 Google 日历。 获得许可后，该功能可以参考用户收件箱中的航班详细信息、晚餐预订或会议日程，以提供量身定制的建议，而无需用户详细说明每个细节。 默认情况下它是关闭的。 Ask Maps 现在还会记住之前的对话，因此用户可以从上次中断的地方继续进行旅行计划。 实时跟踪延误的实时交通小部件也正在推出。

这次更新是谷歌将其产品转变为完成任务而不仅仅是回答问题的代理的最明显例子。 在 5 月份的 I/O 大会上，谷歌用 AI 代理取代了搜索框，这些代理可以监控网络、构建自定义工具并代表用户采取行动。 现在，Ask Maps 在每月有超过 10 亿人使用的导航应用程序中执行同样的操作。 问题是用户是否会信任地图来订购午餐，以及这些交接另一端的餐馆、酒店和票务平台是否会将其视为分销或脱媒。
